candidates.bio: Ottawa-based Jeremy Fisher is a four-time Juno-nominated Canadian folk-pop singer-songwriter whose work spans six studio albums, international touring and the CBC animated series Jeremy and Jazzy.

Cree singer-songwriter Jessa Sky, from Treaty 6 Territory, blends soulful pop, R&B and Indigenous roots with emotionally direct writing about resilience, identity and healing. Since beginning her professional career in 2021, she has earned multiple number-one singles on the Indigenous Music Countdown and was selected for the CBC × SOCAN Reverie Indigenous Music Residency.

Toronto native Jesse Gold is an R&B-pop singer-songwriter, guitarist and producer whose polished, soulful work pairs modern R&B songwriting with musicianship developed from an early age. His catalogue includes the We’ll Be Fine EP and collaborations with artists including JP Saxe, Craig David and Babyface.

Jesse Green Beats is a producer associated with Toronto's independent underground hip-hop scene. His production work includes collaborations with Toronto rappers Asun Eastwood and Lord Juco, including material from their Two Birds project. Northern Dial carries Jesse Green Beats as part of the production network surrounding contemporary Canadian underground rap.

Toronto-born singer-songwriter Jesse Labelle built his career as a pop and country songwriter and performer, moving from local rock bands and collaborations into solo releases and songwriting work in Toronto and Nashville.

Jesse McMillan is a Saskatoon drummer active in the city's jazz, neo-soul and alternative scenes. He has performed with vbnd's Soulmate Collective and with Saskatoon post-punk band Hollow Oax, appearing throughout vbnd's Scum Funk recordings. His drums on vbnd's 2019 single No Other Feeling with Katie Tupper and Connor Newton account for his Northern Dial library credit.
Toronto singer-songwriter and multi-instrumentalist Jessica Sevier blends country, roots and Americana with rock energy and R&B touches in a growing independent Canadian catalogue.

Shelburne, Ontario singer-songwriter Jessica Sole is a Canadian country artist known for polished contemporary production, melodic hooks and an independent career built through radio and live performance.

Jessie Simmons is a Haitian-Canadian singer-songwriter from Ottawa whose music blends R&B and soul with Afro-Caribbean styles including kompa and zouk. Her debut album AMONI won Album of the Year at the Kilimanjaro Music Awards, and she has performed at Canadian Music Week, JunoFest, AfroFest and Ottawa Bluesfest while remaining active in Ottawa's music community.

Jhevon Paris is a Canadian rapper, singer and producer closely associated with Toronto's late-2000s pop, R&B and hip-hop scene. His credits include collaborations with Canadian acts such as Stereos and Divine Brown, along with production and guest-vocal work across major-label Canadian releases. Northern Dial carries Jhevon Paris as part of its Toronto crossover and hip-hop catalogue.
Ontario-born singer-songwriter Jill Barber is a Canadian folk, jazz and pop artist whose English- and French-language recordings have built a long international career.

Jimmie D is a Canadian hip-hop artist from Montreal's St-Henri neighbourhood whose understated, bar-heavy style has become closely associated with producer Nicholas Craven. Their long-running partnership includes projects such as Trout & Brussels Sprouts, Good Man and Good Music Hypnotizes, alongside collaborations with other Canadian underground rappers.

Jimmy Prime is a Toronto rapper and member of the Prime Boys who became closely identified with the city's 2010s hip-hop rise. Raised in Toronto and embedded in the Prime collective, he is widely credited with helping popularize The 6 as a nickname for the city. His appearance alongside SAFE on Smoke Dawg's YND is his Northern Dial library credit.

JJ Adrian is a Vancouver artist, songwriter and producer whose music blends pop, R&B and alternative influences. Creative BC identifies Adrian as a Vancouver artist, and the artist has participated in British Columbia development programs including ARC. Northern Dial carries JJ Adrian as part of its contemporary West Coast catalogue.

JMB Drippy is a Montréal rapper from the Rivière-des-Prairies neighbourhood whose melodic street-rap catalogue includes OK, Ice, Vini Jr and Palmarès. Montréal hip-hop outlet ONZMTL profiled him as a young rapper from RDP, while Quebec music database MUSIQC places him in the province's rap scene. His 2021 collaboration Palmarès with Laval rapper Rach is his Northern Dial library credit.
Calgary-born singer-songwriter Jocelyn Alice is a Canadian pop artist whose solo breakthrough came with the platinum-certified single Jackpot after earlier work in the duo Jocelyn & Lisa.

Toronto-born Joey DeSimone, better known as Joee, is a Canadian dance singer, songwriter and producer who became a fixture of Canadian radio in the late 1990s and early 2000s. His catalogue includes charting singles such as Angel, If I Could, Do You Right and Arriba, and his work earned a JUNO nomination and a SOCAN dance music award.

Dartmouth-based songwriter Joel Plaskett first became nationally visible as a member of Halifax power-pop band Thrush Hermit, whose 1999 album Clayton Park closed one chapter of the city's celebrated 1990s indie-rock era. He moved quickly into solo work and the Joel Plaskett Emergency, using Down at the Khyber and Truthfully Truthfully to establish a catalogue that could move between lean guitar rock, folk, country, lo-fi recording and sharply observed East Coast storytelling.

Plaskett repeatedly turned album structure itself into part of the songwriting. The Emergency's 2007 Ashtray Rock framed teenage memory as a rock-opera narrative, while the three-disc Three expanded his solo writing across 27 songs. Scrappy Happiness was assembled through a song-a-week recording process, and later projects continued to alternate between full-band rock, intimate acoustic work and collaborations, including the folk-rooted Solidarity with his father Bill Plaskett.

His importance to Canadian music is as much regional and infrastructural as commercial. Plaskett has kept Nova Scotia at the centre of his work, toured widely with the Emergency and built Fang Recording in Dartmouth into a home base for his own records and productions for other artists. A 2025 tribute album featuring artists including Arkells, Sloan, City and Colour and Bahamas underscored how deeply his songwriting has travelled through the Canadian independent community.

Nova Scotia rock trio Joel Plaskett Emergency pairs Joel Plaskett's sharp, melodic songwriting with longtime bandmates Dave Marsh and Chris Pennell, carrying East Coast rock and roll through more than two decades of recordings and touring.

John Shambles is the solo project of Kingston, Ontario musician Brett Emmons, best known as the frontman of The Glorious Sons. The project gives Emmons a separate outlet for songwriting beyond the band's catalogue while retaining his roots in Canadian rock. Northern Dial carries John Shambles as part of its contemporary Ontario rock catalogue.
Mississauga-born singer-songwriter Johnny Orlando is a Canadian pop artist who built an early online following before developing a major-label recording and international touring career.
Scottish-born Canadian country and soul singer Johnny Reid grew up in Brampton and built a multi-platinum career around raspy vocals, rootsy songwriting and arena-scale live shows.

Toronto-born and raised rapper Jon Kabongo is a lyricist whose music moves between punchline-heavy boom bap, melodic Afrobeat and more reflective hip-hop. Raised by Congolese immigrant parents in downtown Toronto, he brings that cultural background and his city upbringing into his writing.

Jon McKiel is a New Brunswick songwriter and recording artist whose work moves between guitar music, warped pop and home-studio experimentation. Gold Horatio, released in September 2026, was recorded with Jay Crocker in Baie Verte and Sackville, New Brunswick. The pair handled the arrangements, production and performances themselves, extending a creative partnership that has increasingly shaped McKiel's records. The result is intimate but strange around the edges, with familiar songwriting forms bent by unusual textures and production choices rather than polished smooth.

Joolsannie is the music alias of Halifax/Dartmouth multidisciplinary artist Julia Hutt. She has contributed vocals and co-writing to Aquakultre's Halifax-rooted catalogue, including the 2022 single Lunch, while also working across illustration, video art direction, production and set design. Northern Dial carries Joolsannie as part of its contemporary Atlantic Canadian R&B and independent music catalogue.

Jordan Fall is a Filipino-Canadian rapper, singer and DJ from Toronto whose music blends hip-hop, R&B and electronic influences. After first becoming known behind the decks in Toronto's IXXI circle, including work with Sean Leon, he moved into a solo recording career with releases such as Savings, Good Mourning and Truss.

Canadian alternative hip-hop artist Josh Martinez is a rapper, producer and label founder whose independent career grew through Halifax and Vancouver and includes solo work as well as the duo The Chicharones.
Vancouver singer, songwriter, producer and multi-instrumentalist Josh Ramsay is best known as the frontman of Marianas Trench and as a co-writer and producer on major Canadian pop records.

Edmonton singer-songwriter and multi-instrumentalist Josh Sahunta is a Canadian R&B-pop artist whose melodic, emotionally direct writing has crossed into television placements and adult contemporary audiences. His album To Be Loved Vol. I earned a Juno nomination for Adult Contemporary Album of the Year.

Edmonton hip-hop artist and songwriter Jr. Rhodes, born Brandon D'Souza, blends rap with jazz, neo-soul and melodic production. Emerging from Alberta's independent scene, his catalogue has grown from projects such as Project Paradise into releases including Stuck Between, far from perfect and a waiting king, alongside collaborations with NorthSideBaby and other Edmonton artists.
Halifax-born JRDN, born Ralph Jordon Croucher, is a Canadian R&B singer whose career grew from Nova Scotia's music scene into a Juno-recognized blend of R&B, soul and hip-hop.
Montréal-born Judith Bérard is a Canadian singer-songwriter and actor whose career spans Québec television, pop music and musical theatre, including a long-running turn as Cristal in Starmania.

JUGGER is a Toronto hip-hop artist whose dark, high-energy rap catalogue spans solo work and a long-running creative partnership with Toronto producer WondaGurl. Their 2025 project BABA YAGA 2 includes several of JUGGER's six Northern Dial library tracks, alongside singles such as DIPSET and HELTER SKELTER.

Juice is a Toronto hip-hop artist also known as Rochester or Rochester aka Juice. A longtime figure in the city's rap scene, he has released solo work under both names and has been documented by Canadian music press as a Toronto MC. Northern Dial carries Juice as part of its Toronto hip-hop catalogue.

Jules Halpern is a Toronto pop singer-songwriter whose work spans contemporary pop, soul and theatrical influences. She was among the Canadian performers featured on the 2020 ArtistsCAN benefit recording of Lean on Me and has continued releasing independent singles including Boogiewoman, Hush, Bitchcraft and Stand Beside Me. Northern Dial carries Jules Halpern as part of its contemporary Canadian pop catalogue.

Julian Thomas is a Toronto rapper raised in Etobicoke who has been writing and recording hip-hop since his youth. His work draws on the west-end Toronto environment he grew up in, and he later signed with Sony Music Entertainment Canada while developing a catalogue that blends introspective writing with contemporary rap. Northern Dial carries Julian Thomas as part of its Toronto hip-hop catalogue.

Moncton-born Acadian singer-songwriter Julie Doiron entered Canadian indie-rock history as a teenager in Eric's Trip, playing guitar and then bass as the band developed its mix of melody, distortion and lo-fi intimacy. Formed in New Brunswick in 1990, Eric's Trip became the first Canadian band signed to Seattle's Sub Pop Records, with albums including Love Tara helping establish an Atlantic Canadian branch of the 1990s indie-rock underground. Before the group first split in 1996, Doiron had already begun releasing quieter solo material under the name Broken Girl; she subsequently continued under her own name, carrying the emotional directness of that scene into an increasingly personal songwriting catalogue.

Her solo career quickly proved that the post-Eric's Trip work was more than a side project. Julie Doiron and the Wooden Stars, recorded with the Ottawa band Wooden Stars, won the 2000 JUNO Award for Alternative Album of the Year. She followed with records that moved between fragile folk, noisy guitar music and bilingual songwriting, including the French-language Désormais. The 2007 album Woke Myself Up reunited her with former Eric's Trip bandmates and was shortlisted for the inaugural Polaris Music Prize, while I Can Wonder What You Did with Your Day and So Many Days extended a catalogue built around small observations, domestic detail and songs that can move from near-whisper to full-band distortion without losing their intimacy.

Doiron's importance also comes from the network around that catalogue. She has collaborated with artists including Gordon Downie, the Tragically Hip, Mount Eerie and Okkervil River, linking Atlantic Canadian indie rock to wider folk, experimental and singer-songwriter communities. After a long gap between solo albums, 2021's I Thought of You returned to a louder band setting and demonstrated how naturally her early indie-rock instincts still fit the plainspoken writing she developed over decades. That continuity makes Doiron a connective figure in Canadian independent music: part of a landmark Sub Pop band, a JUNO-winning solo artist and a songwriter whose understated influence extends well beyond one scene or era.

Formed in Toronto in 2010, July Talk built its identity around contrast. Peter Dreimanis's rough baritone and Leah Fay's clearer, more elastic voice turn songs into conversations, arguments and negotiations, while the band's early music drew from garage rock, blues and indie rock. Their self-titled debut arrived in 2012 and grew through touring into a national breakthrough, eventually going gold in Canada and winning the 2015 JUNO for Alternative Album of the Year.

The group expanded that tension on Touch, which included "Push + Pull" and a collaboration with Tanya Tagaq on "Beck + Call." Rather than treating the dual-frontperson setup as a visual gimmick, July Talk made questions of power, intimacy and performance central to both the songs and its famously physical live shows. Pray for It followed in 2020 and earned another JUNO for Alternative Album of the Year, confirming that the band's initial impact had developed into sustained critical recognition.

Remember Never Before arrived in 2023 with a more spacious, synth-aware version of the band's sound while preserving the vocal friction at its centre. July Talk's significance within Canadian alternative rock lies in how thoroughly performance and songwriting reinforce one another: the band created an instantly identifiable stage language, then built enough musical depth around it to remain a major Canadian live and recording act for more than a decade.

Junk is a Vancouver rapper with German, Italian and Canadian roots whose career spans independent hip-hop, battle rap and collaborative releases. He is also associated with Vancouver's Household Records community. Northern Dial carries Junk as part of its West Coast Canadian hip-hop catalogue.

Junkhouse emerged from Hamilton at the start of the 1990s and became one of the bands that gave the city's rootsy, hard-edged rock tradition a national platform. Singer-songwriter Tom Wilson formed the group in 1989 with guitarist Dan Achen, drummer Ray Farrugia and bassist Russ Wilson; later members included Colin Cripps and Grant Marshall. After several years of club work, Junkhouse signed with Sony Music Canada and released Strays in 1993. The album's mix of blues, roots rock and alternative-rock weight produced the international single "Out of My Head" and established the group well beyond the Southern Ontario circuit where it had developed.

The band followed with Birthday Boy in 1995 and Fuzz in 1997. Birthday Boy broadened the group's sound and included "Burned Out Car," a collaboration with Sarah McLachlan. Across those records, Junkhouse occupied a useful middle ground in 1990s Canadian rock: heavier and more ragged than polished adult alternative, but deeply connected to blues, roots music and the Hamilton songwriting community. That identity made the group distinct from the many Canadian acts chasing the grunge and post-grunge sounds dominating radio at the time.

Junkhouse eventually dissolved as its members moved into other work, but its legacy spread through those later careers. Wilson went on to Blackie and the Rodeo Kings and Lee Harvey Osmond, while Achen became an important producer and studio figure in Hamilton before his death in 2010. The band's three-album run remains an important link between the city's older roots-rock culture and the nationally visible Hamilton scenes that followed. Junkhouse matters not simply as a 1990s radio act, but as part of the infrastructure and lineage of a city with an unusually deep Canadian rock identity.

Korean-Canadian singer-songwriter and producer JUNNY grew up in Vancouver before relocating to South Korea, where his smooth R&B-pop work expanded into songwriting for major K-pop artists including NCT, IU and Baekhyun.

Scarborough rapper and art curator John Samuels, known as Just John, is a Toronto creative whose forward-looking hip-hop grew alongside his Blank Canvas arts collective and later collaborations with producer Dom Dias.

Canadian guitarist, singer-songwriter and producer Justice Der is based in Toronto, where his fluid instrumental style blends jazz, hip-hop, alternative and ambient music. He first built a large online following through guitar covers before expanding into original projects and collaborations with artists including Rachel Bobbitt.
American-born, Toronto-raised singer-songwriter Justin Nozuka is a Canadian-American artist whose intimate catalogue blends folk, soul, R&B and acoustic songwriting.

Jxggi is a Brampton-based Punjabi-Canadian rapper whose melodic hip-hop catalogue includes They Don't Know, Big Plays, Breaking Boundaries and Inferno. HipHopCanada has covered him as a Canadian-based Punjabi artist, while Apple Music describes him as a Punjabi Canadian rapper. Why Me?, his 2025 collaboration with AR Paisley and Sickboi from the 4 Real EP, is his Northern Dial library credit.

Toronto rapper, songwriter and producer K-Fresh, later known as Knemesis, has worked across music and visual production in the city’s hip-hop scene. His early credits include the posse cut Get It Right from JB’s My Environment before he continued releasing solo material and directing music videos under the Knemesis name.

Born in Mogadishu, Somalia and raised partly in Toronto after his family fled civil war, K'NAAN developed a form of hip-hop shaped by migration, oral storytelling and the memory of a country he had left behind. His 2005 debut, The Dusty Foot Philosopher, paired detailed accounts of war, displacement and immigrant life with rap, African instrumentation and live-band arrangements. The album won the JUNO Award for Rap Recording of the Year and was shortlisted for the inaugural Polaris Music Prize.

K'NAAN widened that sound on 2009's Troubadour, recorded with an international cast while keeping Somali experience at the centre of his writing. Its song “Wavin' Flag” became a global anthem after a remixed version was selected for Coca-Cola's 2010 FIFA World Cup campaign; a separate Young Artists for Haiti recording featuring Canadian performers reached No. 1 in Canada. The song's enormous reach sometimes overshadowed the more complex political and autobiographical work surrounding it.

His importance to Canadian music is larger than a single crossover hit. K'NAAN helped make refugee experience, African diasporic identity and Toronto's Somali community visible within mainstream Canadian hip-hop, while demonstrating that an artist could move between personal testimony, international pop and explicitly political writing without treating those modes as separate careers.

Pioneering Toronto MC Shawn 'K-4ce' Morrison is an early architect of the city's hip-hop identity, remembered for coining the term 'T-Dot' and for work with artists including Michie Mee, Maestro Fresh Wes and Ghetto Concept. Raised between Toronto's Weston neighbourhood and New York City, he helped shape the vocabulary and culture of Toronto rap before the city's later international breakthrough.

Vancouver producer and DJ K-Rec, born Kent Stephany, is a longtime figure in Canadian underground hip-hop whose sample-driven production and turntablism have connected generations of West Coast rap artists.

K.C. Thomas is a Toronto hip-hop artist connected to the Circle collective and Choclair's early independent catalogue. K.C. Thomas appears alongside Afrolistic on What It Takes (Ill B. Mix), a key recording from Toronto's 1990s rap scene. Northern Dial carries K.C. Thomas as part of that early Canadian hip-hop lineage.
